search_log: Searched “There There Tommy Orange excerpt publisher first second third person chapters” and related excerpt/POV queries; found the licensed BookBrowse opening and Penguin Random House book and reader-guide pages.
Searched for scholarly discussion of the novel’s narrative structure and second-person narration; opened the UCLA dissertation and inspected its whole-book structural analysis.

Searched reviews for explicit first-, second-, and third-person descriptions; opened the Star Tribune review, Penguin Random House Common Reads author Q&A, Wikipedia overview, and LitCharts style page.

The Penguin Random House product page and reader’s guide confirmed twelve characters and different voices/perspectives but did not independently enumerate all grammatical persons; they were used for discovery rather than as standalone person evidence.
person_note: The novel has sustained base sections in multiple persons. The quotes independently expose participating first-person singular and plural narration and story-specific second-person narration; brief he/she passages were conservatively left unmarked because their local context is insufficient to prove third person. Whole-book scholarly analysis, an author Q&A hosted by the publisher, and a substantive review establish that other character chapters use sustained third-person narration as well. Gnomic prologue/interlude statements and dialogue were not allowed to vote mechanically, although the licensed opening confirms the prologue’s collective first-person voice. The channels therefore agree on ALTERNATING, with no credible contrary evidence and no material remaining uncertainty.
